newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen up, extends Thursday's rise.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen up, extends Thursday's rise.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open higher Friday, extending yesterday's rise linked to expectation of increased air conditioning demand in the Southwest.
"It looks strong and wants to go higher," said one New York futures broker. "Apparently, there's a short-squeeze going on here," he added.

In over-the-counter business, May California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were quoted at $13.50-13.60 a megawatt hour (MWh) versus yesterday's close of $13.29 and May Palo Verde (PV) at $17.25-17.50 against previous day's settlement of $16.95.
The 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon nuclear unit 1 on the central California coast is scheduled to shut Saturday for a 36-day refueling and maintenance outage.
The Diablo Canyon outage would be offset by increased hydroelectric production in the Northwest with rising snowmelt and runoffs due to warming temperatures, market sources said.
If May PV falters, the contract will likely fill the trading gap between $16.50 and $16.75, which was formed yesterday.

Meterologists said temperatures across the Southwest would run four to 12 degrees Fahrenheit above normal into next Wednesday, while those in the Northwest would average two to six degrees F above normal through the weekend.
The 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 nuclear power unit remained shut for refueling and maintenance, with an expected restart date in late June.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant in Washington state was also shut for refueling, and was expected to resume power output in early July.
In addition, nearly 6,000 MW of thermal generating capacity was off-line in the West for planned and unplanned maintenance as well as hydropower displacement sales.
